text: A horse! A horse! An acceptable amount of florins for a horse!
Steel barding adds that certain something to your mount. A pity they didn't have it in red.

During the Siege of Remas, a cannonball flew straight at Borgio. Instead of rather influential smithereens, bystanders witnessed that the projectile was stuck right into the Prince's armour, who was barely wounded. Melted and reshaped as a mace, the cannonball makes for a terrifying and symbolic weapon.
During the most furious melees, Borgio wears his frightening mask, a grotesque grimace of malice. Coupled with the wearer's bulk and might, the effect is scary indeed.
Only some scholars might know what those statues were about, but once melted and used to forge this huge brazen armour, they might have brought over whatever enchantment they used to bear...
Borgio has always cared for the needs of his troops, even the lowest mercs, and minded where they deployed them. Trust goes both ways.
Battles are a matter of applying force to the weakest point. The tougher the force, the louder the crack.
Ogres, Greenskins, Chaos Worshippers, all shall be punished for the destruction they perpetrate against Gashnagia.
The fall of Ushoran's empire burns vivid in Gashnag's cultivated memories. The other bloodlines are not to be trusted, not even fellow Strigoi.
Led from the front by their powerful and selfless Prince, the citizens of Gashnagia fight like one.
Promoting conservative tactics, Gashnag preserves his subject's safety until melee is inevitable.
Seeding constant confusion among the opponents, the Black Prince protects his subjects from harm.
Know thy enemy, and fight it with its own tools.
Divine worship aside, Ushoran's empire was still fundamentally happy and loyal, which is fairly uncommon on its own right.
Even in his delusions, Gashnag knows that he doesn't need to conquer more lands to keep his own happy. Even if the neighbours don't know what they're talking to.
Everything stands on Gashnag not being recognized for what he is. As such, mages and agents have to be kept at a safe distance.
Knowledge is power, and this learning comes from the Strigoi patriarch's secrets and mistakes.
One of Ushoran's own artefacts, this polestaff supposedly allowed the original Strigoi patriarch to hold out the Lahmians' aggression for so long.

It is said that a town ruled by Gashnag was being harassed by a group of Ogres. The Black Prince set out on his own, beneath his black cloak, and came back with the pillagers' heads, to be put on pikes.
Ride with me? In broad daylight? Dear, you are far too unimportant for that.
A false promise here, a shift of alliances there, and the enemy has no idea it's not an ally anymore.
Discreetly poisoning the enemy commanders the night before battle is... well, just another continuation of diplomacy, like war itself.
Another secret recipe of Lucrezzia's, this concoction will greatly improve the imbiber's strength and resilience. Maybe, just maybe, also poison them. A bit.
The Lady of Pavona is famous, among other things, for kissing the weapon of today's champion before his duel or battle. Of course, her lipstick is terribly poisonous.
Lucrezzia always wears, somewhere on her person, a dagger coated with another of her brews. Can't blame someone for being prepared for a midnight stab.
Lucrezzia's manipulation over military champions and leaders leads to survival of the fittest.

The previous seven husbands of Lucrezzia's have always been useful and influential men, until they stopped being such. During these dire circumstances of exile, the new consort must be especially... supportive.

Tibaldus Marsarius de Vela, current Prince of Tobaro and powerful banker. His city is a safe port and cosmopolitan center that is certainly very promising in the right hands. However, Magritta's rulers would feel threatened.
Marrying the eccentric ruler of Magritta would make for an interesting life and a hand on the wheel of the powerful city, but it would also antagonize Lucrezzia's Tilean compatriots.
...Or maybe not. Having a lot of suitors, especially the influential ones, may open a lot more doors than only one.
Most things simply do not stand for long when Borgio is set to conquer them.
Very personal aggressors find out too late that it is not easy to stab a powerful Strigoi cloaked in illusions.
Every rose has its thorn. This one in particular, a handy dagger and several hired guardians as well.

Lucrezzia may consolidate her relationship with Xavier Rothemuur, current ruler of the northern port and expatriate member of House Rothemuur of Marienburg. Lucrezzia would secure the support of not one, but two wealthy City-States, but the other rulers of Estalia may definitely perceive her as a threat.
A rare arabyan Pegasus, gifted by Crusaders. A living and swift siphon of light and magic, ready to unleash their energy on aggressors.
A Dwarf's grudge is forever, but so is his gratitude for many lives saved. The unexpected gift of a family runic axe is to be remembered for just as long.

Formerly a magic and fluttering arabyan turban, this souvenir bears energetic enchantments. The cadre of Myrmidian priests who prodded it for a week have testified that the scarf won't strangle Gausser of its own initiative anytime soon, which is oddly specific.

A horse! A horse! An acceptable amount of florins for a horse!
I had actually sent to buy a unicorn. Made of diamonds. Like, a real live unicorn made of diamonds, very stylish. But they say it can't be done. Unimaginative buggers, the lot of them.
Lupio's own demigryph owes his companionship to Lupio and "Big Magpie" nickname to his distinctive black and white coat and attraction towards shiny baubles.
An ancient elven blade, relic of a time when Tilea was an Asur colony. Its wielder's attacks leave a glowing and elegant trail of light and molten armour.
Catrazza is not usually one for religious displays, but there are solid practical and diplomatical advantages for wearing this ring around.
A cloak made of Lustrian gold, with uncertain magic properties. Its known feature is to give Lupio immense satisfaction.
Reaped during a confusing skirmish against reptiles, elf corsairs and marauders, this ring bears an eerie and intriguing aura over it. Inquisitors never managed to get it off Lupio for investigation.
Magrittan naval prowess accepts very few rivals. Begrudgingly.
Estalians are notoriously fascinated by the gold overseas. Lupio is more interested in the gold over himself.
They stink, and really they don't know any better than living in muddy shacks. Also, something should be done about their wretched windmills.
Perfect uniforms and incessant drills, that's the stuff.

Lupio has secretly concocted the perfect plan to dramatically improve the region's welfare. This requires him to destroy all windmills in the world, particularly those that move by themselves. Despite people telling Lupio those are Giants, they clearly don't know better.
Catrazza's companies have gathered much fame as reliable and efficient skirmishers, able to bring victory against all odds.
It is good to be friends with most of the armed nobles of the region, and to always know who was in whose bedroom.
Once again, Tilea will be covered in marble and, most importantly, wealthy in money and people.
The Very Best Money Can Buy
Good equipment may make the difference between competent and successful mercenaries, or competent and dead ones. Everything is an investment towards the future.
The so-called Birdmen of Catrazza (no relations) are a weird lot, to be sure, but they are good at scouting and at getting out of tight spots.
Being considered a true friend by the Dwarfs is a huge honour and benefit. As long as one keeps being careful not to offend them.
Good warriors and equipment coming from the mountains, not only the poorest dwarf misfits and adventurers caught at a low ebb.
Sincere Dwarf warriors will defend your kin like their own. And teach your own fighters to fight like they do.
Gods know the Dwarfs are careful with their trade relationships. Especially with related payments. Favoured ties are to be cherished.

You shoulda seen him! There was the troll behind him, right, raising its club, then Beardy turns around and buries his axe right in the thing's face! And down it goes! Who would have known dem damn stunties can move that quickly? Oh, hey Beardy!
Money equals power, power equals money. Marinated in good manners and leverage, money can move mountains aside. And armies, especially armies.
Good handguns are the future of warfare, if only these wretched peasants wouldn't whine so much about having to pay for them.
Men will always gather around the leader that is fighting for the well-being of their own country.
El Cadavo is a feared and inspiring figure in three continents. However, some would rather snuff his existence altogether.

It is with one of nature's tricks that Cadavo created one Duke Arrenault's hardship. It was El Cadavo, still in Tilea, that originally happened to destroy Rodrigo Delmonte's lands, which in turn prompted the latter to start what ended up as the Alcatani Fellowship. In one of the company's campaigns, it was Duke Arrenault's turn to fall in the dust, losing his knights, his feud and his eye to the Tilean pikes. A fallen knight by fate and attitude, Arrenault goes renegade in search for the tools for vengeance.

Arrenault is in Estalia, trying to gather what men and resources he can against the Alcatani and their masters. He is out of luck until he is mistaken for the famous El Cadavo, whose successful persona he promptly abuses to lead what turns out being an overseas expedition. Arrenault ends up in the New World, growing into the figure of a ruthless mercenary commander, accruing a large retinue of adventurers and even other disillusioned Bretonnians. Almost as he reckoned his resources to be enough for his vendetta, the real Cadavo, also in the New World, gets wind of the impostor. El Cadavo and Arrenault start a slithery game of hunted and hunter until their forces collide under a showering monsoon. The battle is fierce and chaotic, yet the two leaders finally manage to meet each other in a fierce and one-eyed duel in the undergrowth. In the exhausted silence of a dying battle, a fateful pistol shot rings among the rain sprays.

Renegades, adventurers and mercenaries stop fighting as one, as the monsoon also stops its apparently tireless attempt at turning the place into a swamp. A couple of minutes later, Cadavo emerges from the jungle, bloodied yet satisfied, for the challenger is dead, head caved in by the bullet. He raises Arrenault's crest, the trophy upon which he scratches his victory mark, as the survivors from both armies cheer the victor, for this is how things often go among such fighters. He adds the crest to the lot of other charms and trophies he carries, and reassembles his troops for whatever the future awaits.

Only a few of the defeated are killed: there aren't many other ways to get rid of troublemakers so far away from provisions and what passes as civilization. And yet the survivors' hearts are high, because even if the day was bloody and wet, the pay is going to be excellent, the future looks bright for they are the best troops ever assembled in the Colonies, under a legendary Condottiero that has just defeated an upstart rival and that now only intends to restock and start what promises to be a fruitful adventure in a ripe land.

That he would lead the greatest adventuring army ever assembled, that he would trample any opposition in this New World and in the Old World. That he would never forget his past and learn from it, for the future challenges will likely demand each grain of his ability.

That he is El Cadavo, the greatest mercenary commander to ever exist, a rock against the ebbs and tides of the ruthless world, and that he will be just as merciless for the world is his for the taking, and for anybody who would follow him to glory.

A Duke was just another notch on Cadavo's blades, just another scar on his face. The figure of Cadavo was born in the heat of politics and battle, had matured in incredible stories and then into myth. The clever would notice that Cadavo's stories are centuries old, scattered in space and time and yet mostly true. Someone whispers that he is immortal, that his is only a title, that he cannot just be a mercenary commander. Be that as it may, Arrenault's apparent demise will just fuel Cadavo's legend and add another paragraph to fireside stories.
Cadavo's current steed is an ill-tempered gelding only loyal and tending to Cadavo. To those few he doesn't kick on sight, he answers to the name of Broccolo.
It doesn't matter if they have gambling issues or if their perception of property is somewhat challenged. These men are the best fighters around Cadavo.
Cadavo's usual bunch also tends to dispatch opponents as quickly as possible, since in a dangerous New World the least dangerous foe is a trained Elf. Or maybe they just like hurting stuff.
Whatever the enemy, Cadavo is unsubtle in his subtlety and will exploit any possible trick to vex the enemy. His troops are veteran harriers and have learned from the best.
Cadavo has survived multiple military campaigns, an undefined number of duels, at least five magical armageddons and six mothers-in-law.
An amulet made of a weird alloy, capable of neutralizing poisons and many of the magical properties for weapons that would injure the bearer.

A lucky prey from a skirmish against Corsairs, this rare magical repeater crossbow is too cumbersome for use on foot, but if you want something positively dead, it's a nice toy. Just have to hope the magic in it isn't too dark.
This baby can do zero to fifty in nothing! And I swear she can understand everything I- did she just write sixty" with her hoof?"
Yes, I can see that is a Minotaur skull, my day hasn't improved one bit.
That's a rat, right? Yes, that's a rat. I was worried you'd say that.
It's Corsairs again, boys. Say your prayers and remember they run faster than you do.
That's a pretty good impression of an orc, alright. We can do that, pal, just show us where they are.
Franco, I know you have only the one arm left, but if they say there are Chaos fellas around here it's everybody's problem, alright?
A skull. Walks like a drunk. Bites. Huinipachutli, mate, unless you're mimicking Giovanni I know what you mean.
Making friends with Skink interpreters isn't easy, but the more contacts you have, the more you understand each other, the more business can be done.
Skink Priests like their prophetic mumbo-jumbo, but their needs are just as businesslike as anybody else's. And they pay in pearls as big as their eyes.
Managing to get an audience with an actual Slann is a big honour, to actually get them to notice you in those big fat plans of theirs is... a triumph.
Surprisingly, the local Slanns and Chiefs seem legitimately friendly now towards Colombo's expedition. There is a lot to learn just by being shown around their cities.
Fine troops, personally drilled by Colombo, tend to become a devastating force on the battlefield.
Colombo's fame, and his army's, is growing. Even the most fearsome bandits and raiders tend to shuffle their feet upon learning they have become a target for Colombo's mercenaries.
Marco Colombo is famous for having 'discovered' the New World, and for being one of the very few to have peaceful dealings with the Lizardmen.
A reward from the Slann, this amulet in the shape of Sotek's tongue feels oddly alive and protected the wearer more times than he recalls.
About as potent as orange juice to the Lizardmen, this precious lustrian wine is strong indeed for a human!
Used by someone to write an otherwise uninteresting map, this scroll bears potent enchantments of Nehekharan protective magic. However, it tends to crumble a bit with each use.
Cadavo will have his city. The fat toad will probably get tired of destroying it way before Cadavo is of trying.
Until he is usurped, for these things tend to happen in Tilea and especially in Trantio, Colombo is still prince, with friends over there. Armoured friends.
You take care of your mates, and they take care of you.
You may not like it, but this is what peak performance looks like.
Borgio knows the worth of a well-trained and well-protected force of versatile crossbowmen. Let Miragliano be known for a fearsome force of troops that can block well, fight well and shoot back!
Borgio has no time for being wounded by his enemies. Not even by forks.
Oh, so much can be done with a letter here, a smile there, or more audacious initiatives. The Lady of Pavona's ability to maintain her web of connections is powerful and precious in this world.

Gashnag allows a few well-controlled ghouls and beasts to circle around his forces, attacking his foes and his foes only. Even if the wretched creatures are incredibly well-behaved for their type and ultimately fight on the humans' side, old habits die hard and many start connecting the dots.
Some people mistake Lupio's battlefield antics for astute shows of force and bravery for the troops. Truth is, they're Lupio's own satisfaction.
Catrazza's political skills and calm demeanour has led a few to forget he once was an able captain of venture, and a quick fencer at that.

Eustaquio's presence at the lead of an army has an understandably perplexing effect on the troops, except on the most travelled of them. Some who have taken up odd customs abroad even tried to paint a pair of moustaches on the skull.

The old Sunscryer trusts the fellow human so very marginally more than he trusts the other races, and any common ground only propels his paranoia. Something about their foreigner habits and their filthy lingo.

Unbeknownst to him, Sokth's curse pervading what is left of his body is only becoming stronger, more vengeful and contagious. Eventually, it will put an end to Eustaquio's unlife, but until then it's only corroborating his belief in a blessing of the gods.
These End Times of yours, pffsh, the crops are not even failing that much. When I was young I had to fight off two thousand Arabyans just to get to my hors- WHERE ARE YOU GOING?
Be like a spear, and have a point! Ah-ah!
The rulers of Luccini may be eccentric and a bit inbred, but Lorenzo is a great fighter at the head of the best pikes of Tilea.
Lupo likes to run to the edge of his Principality and back to the other border. And again.
Oh my gods, but here goes Lorenzo with the Double Elbow Bonanza! What a match!
In one of the bloodiest pages of Tilean culture, the true mettle of a warrior is measured in the pit, for the amusement of the public. And Lorenzo is very entertaining.
Mate of mine saw the Prince in the baths. He said he had an eight pack. Lorenzo is shredded.
Row row row your boat, they used to say, and Lorenzo can sweat and pull for miles.
Lorenzo may be a weird fellow with his obsession for the antiques and the ancients, but his physique surely reminds one of the impossibly-perfect statues literring Luccini.
Luccini commands the strongest fleet in Tilea and perhaps the strongest army as well.
They say that Luccinians will depose a Prince with poor humour. They take jokes seriously over there.
Nothing shines as bright as the man in gilted armour who insists on having telescopes aimed at himself.

Such unrivalled talent, unmitigated brilliance, unparalleled strategy, a pig destined to rule and lead to a new golden age. \\nOr so his guardians say, as they translate Piggolo's every though, move and project.
So very efficient, my lord. \\n"Why didn't we think of that before?"
Your presence has certainly gotten majestic and, err, enormous, my lord. \\n"Girthy." \\n"Heroic!"
My lord, not in ther- oh, gods, not again.\\n"Fetch the Bath Guard with buckets this instant!"
They shall tremble at your mere sight, my prince.
Indeed, my lord, they will fire at will and with efficiency if they value their double pay!

Another one, my lord?\\n"I swear, it's like truffles."
We haven't seen such military prowess since Prince Borgio!\\n"You do know he's alive, yes?"
